items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — call had no structure from the opening on
Customer volunteered he is a repeat Einstein customer ('I've used you guys in the past') — rep never pulled or recapped the prior move or any details on file
Never asked the move date and never checked availability, despite the customer saying his condo closing is Monday
Customer said outright 'I just need this stuff packed' — rep never acknowledged or scoped packing services, box counts, or packing materials
313 W 17th St Unit 1404 is a downtown high-rise — never asked about elevator, floor, loading dock, parking, walk distance, or HOA/COI requirements
No stairs/floors, additional rooms, additional stops, or special-considerations probing
Customer said 'I have no idea what to do' — clear moving-stressor cue, never acknowledged or explored
Zero pricing delivered: no 'pricing is super simple' opener, no hourly rate, no what's-included list, no disassembly/reassembly, no packing pricing, no 'no hidden fees' pitch
No No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee — insurance was only mentioned as the reason he can't load a pod
No clock explanation at all — no on-site start, no 2.5 hour minimum, no 15-minute increments, no sense-check
No estimate: no time range for a 1400 sqft two-bedroom, no mover/truck count, no variables (elevator, walk distance, drive time to storage, packing time)
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no prep-lowers-the-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
No attempt to lock a date or book — let a live, time-pressured repeat customer hang up to go call storage companies with no follow-up time, no callback commitment, and nothing in EMMA
No 'any other questions before I let you go?', no hours or how to reach us, no bolded-details/reply-with-corrections email framing
Used the customer's name only once and closed with 'For sure not a problem' — no warm farewell or thank you
top_strength: He handled the third-party-load question honestly and clearly, explaining the insurance reason Einstein won't load a pod and then re-flagging it a second time so the customer wasn't surprised later. The Sparefoot referral with a concrete 10x15/10x20 size recommendation for a 1400 sqft home was genuinely useful, specific help.
coaching_note: The moment the customer said 'if that's a possibility' to loading into a storage unit, this stopped being a referral call and became a bookable job — a 1400 sqft two-bedroom load-out with packing, closing Monday, from a repeat customer. Lukas instead let him hang up to go shop storage units with no price, no date, and no callback. The fix: once the customer accepts a service you can perform, pivot straight into the standard flow — confirm the move date and availability first, then quote the hourly rate and what's included, then say 'go find your unit, I'll hold Monday and email you everything now.' Storage sizing help is worth nothing if the job walks.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and responsive with light affirmations ('there shouldn't be an issue whatsoever', 'for sure not a problem'), but transactional throughout — no name use beyond confirming the spelling, no empathy when the customer said he had no idea what to do, and the policy explanations ran long and circular.
audio_review_reason: Transcript quality is poor and may be understating him — garbled stretches ('give me a sec where that's much okay'), 'pod' repeatedly rendered as 'pot', and the speaker labels are wrong (the customer is tagged 'Deana Melendez' but identifies himself as Ross Melby). Worth an audio listen to confirm the flat/rambling read and to verify the caller's identity for CRM matching.
